transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't keep my mind on my actual experiments anymore. It's getting to be a real problem at the lab. 

Like, I'll be in the middle of a grant call or a safety meeting, and I'll notice something completely minor—a pump vibration, or a student's side comment, or maybe I'll just think of some odd peak in an old data spectrum. And suddenly, I'm just off chasing that for hours. Meanwhile, the actual work, the thing everyone actually needs from me, just completely falls apart.

Can you describe what happens when you get distracted by these minor things? Do you find it hard to pull yourself back to the main task, or do you get completely absorbed in the new thing that caught your attention?

I get completely absorbed. It's... well, I don't really pull myself back at all. 

Once my brain latches onto that pump vibration, or whatever it is, I'm just gone. I'll spend hours running down some rabbit hole, looking up old manuals or taking things apart, and I don't even think about the main task again until someone actually comes looking for me to ask where my report is. I just completely lose track of what I was supposed to be doing.
When these distractions take over, do you feel a strong sense of urgency or like you absolutely have to follow through on them right away?

Not really... I wouldn't call it a sense of urgency. It's not like I feel this intense pressure that I absolutely have to look into it right that second. 

It's more just... my brain completely switches gears. The new thing just becomes the only thing in front of me, and I completely forget the original task even existed. So there isn't really a panic or a driven feeling to it, I just get completely sidetracked without even realizing I've dropped the ball on everything else.

Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was extremely high or low—like feeling unusually energetic, elated, or irritable for days at a time, or feeling deeply depressed or hopeless for weeks?

Yes, I have. For months now, I've felt... well, unusually energetic, I guess. It feels like the lab is finally moving at my speed. Everything just feels almost electrified to me. 

But the irritable part you mentioned—that's definitely there too. If someone questions my plan, or if they ask me to just slow down a bit, I just snap at them. I don't really mean to, but I do. It's actually gotten to the point where my students have started avoiding my office completely.
When did these feelings of being unusually energetic and irritable start, and have they been continuous or have they come and gone in distinct periods?

It's been continuous. This has been going on for about seven months now, ever since I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project. It hasn't really stopped or faded since then, just this constant hum.

During this seven-month period, have you ever felt that your energy or activity levels were so high that you didn't need much sleep, or that you could do multiple things at once without tiring? Did others notice that you were acting unusually—maybe talking more quickly, taking risks, or starting a lot of new projects at once?

Yes, definitely on the activity level. I'm at the lab before anyone else even arrives in the morning. And I'm just doing so much at once—I'll be rewriting protocols, rearranging the instrument schedules, emailing our collaborators in three different countries, and starting up new analyses all at the exact same time. 

I don't really get tired doing it, either. It's just... if I sit still, it feels like I'm wasting the one chance I have to actually fix everything. So I just keep going.

Have you had any periods where your mood was elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four days in a row—where it was clearly different from your usual mood and other people might have noticed a change in you?

Well, like I said, it hasn't really been just four days. It's been this way constantly for the last seven months. I haven't really had any breaks from it. It's just been this one long stretch since I took over the project.

Can you recall a specific time when your mood was so elevated or irritable that it was clearly different from how you usually feel, and people around you noticed that you were acting out of character?

Well, like I was saying, it's been going on for months now. I just feel like the lab is finally moving at my speed, you know? It's almost like I'm electrified. But... yeah, if someone questions my plan or tells me I need to slow down, I just snap at them. It's out of character for me, but I can't help it. It's actually gotten to the point where I've noticed some of the students are actively avoiding my office.
